caveats: XGBoost hyperparameters (config/risk_policy.json) were tuned in the notebook on an 80/20 split that overlaps these CV test folds, so XGBoost rows are slightly optimistic (no nested CV).
The cost threshold is chosen on the same pooled out-of-fold PDs it is evaluated on; compare it with the Bayes-optimal threshold 1/(1+cost_ratio), which uses no data.
Grade boundaries are policy (config/risk_policy.json); grade counts pool all 5 repeats, so each firm appears 5 times.
Recall at a fixed 0.50 threshold is not comparable across uncalibrated models; compare ROC-AUC / PR-AUC.

xgboost_params.scale_pos_weight: n_negative / n_positive of each training fold

altman_z_benchmark.score: -Z (lower Z = higher risk), raw ratios, Altman 1968 coefficients
altman_z_benchmark.caveat: Ratios are 0-1 normalised in this dataset, so Z values and the 1.81/2.99 zones are not interpretable; only the ranking (AUC) is reported.

calibration.rule: isotonic only if its mean paired Brier gain over sigmoid exceeds the std of that gain
calibration.how: CalibratedClassifierCV(ensemble=False) with a 5-fold inner CV inside each outer training fold

nested.label: NESTED CV: tuning, calibration choice and threshold choice all happen inside each outer training fold

inner.calibration_rule: isotonic only if its mean paired Brier gain over sigmoid exceeds the std of that gain (inner 5-fold)
inner.threshold: minimise expected cost at 10:1 on inner out-of-fold calibrated PDs

nested.grades_note: Grades are rank-ordered (observed default rate rises with grade); they are not a calibration claim. Compare mean_predicted_pd with observed_default_rate per grade. Counts pool all repeats.
